name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+32 partisan lean makes this one of the most Democratic districts in the country

Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but no sign of a real shift in the seat's partisanship

model.rationale: The district's 32-point Democratic lean dominates the outlook even with the incumbent off the ballot after a primary upset; markets price the Democratic nominee at 96 percent, and the Republican shows no fundraising footprint.
model.watch: Only a historic national Republican wave or an unforeseen collapse in Democratic nominee support would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 13th District, covering upper Manhattan and parts of the Bronx, is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 32 points. Adriano Espaillat lost renomination, so the general election will not feature the incumbent, but the seat's fundamentals overwhelmingly favor the party that holds it. Darializa Avila Chevalier emerged from an expensive primary, raising about $1.6 million and drawing nearly $1.9 million in outside support, while Republican Jomo Williams shows no reported fundraising or outside spending.

Prediction markets price the Democrat at 96 percent to win, and with no general-election polling or expert ratings available, the outlook rests on the district's overwhelming partisan makeup. A Republican win would require a historic realignment in a district where Democrats routinely win by wide margins. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
